items.evidence: README play command (--ticks 2 --seed 1 --settings fresh) printed one JSON object at screen title with all 39 keys of the brief (tick..records), no-season defaults as the brief says.
--frame f_title.png --size 800x480 (and 12 other frames) wrote PNGs; header reads 800 x 480.

Fresh title texts [Day Market, New season, Records, Stamps, Settings, Quit], menu_index 0; up at 0 stays 0, down x7 stops at 4; enter on Quit at tick 5 froze the run (30-tick run printed tick 6, screen title).

Settings start 'Language: English','Difficulty: Normal','Season: 7 days'; left at English stays, right->es then stops; difficulty left->easy, right x3 -> hard and stops; season right->3 days, stops, left->7; Escape and Enter on Back return to title.
Run 1 with --settings k1 set es/easy/3; run 2 on k1 started with es, easy, 3. Fresh folder: en/normal/7, slots [null,null,null], stamps [], records [].

In es: title, slots ('Ranura 1: Vacia'), settings (switches at once on Right), records ('Aun no hay records'), stamps, morning ('No hay monedas suficientes', 'Pedido aceptado'), stall, day, paused ('En pausa','Seguir','Titulo'), evening ('Pedido entregado','Sello: ...','Quiebra'), upgrades ('comprada'), season over ('Puntos') all Spanish; en.json and es.json have the same keys.
modules/work/data/en.json and es.json hold the strings, one per language; README 'Adding a language' says how.
New season on fresh: texts [New season, Slot 1: Empty, Slot 2: Empty, Slot 3: Empty]; escape -> title.
seed 1 enter,enter: screen morning, day 1, slot 1, coins 50, rep 50, every stock [], prices 4/6/11/14/7/9, upgrades [], crate_limit 8, order null, texts Morning, Day 1 of 7, Coins: 50.

Easy+3 days -> coins 60, 'Day 1 of 3', forecast 3 entries; Hard -> coins 40. Continue after settings changed to easy/7 kept season_difficulty normal/length 7 in the restored season (slots entry keeps its own difficulty).
forecast has 7 (or 3) entries from sun/cloud/rain/heat; seed 3 days 1-4 weather sun, rain, cloud, heat = forecast and 'Weather:' text; seed 3 run twice gives same forecast.
Wholesale over seeds 1-5 and days 2-4 all within base-1..base+2; rows like 'Apples: 2 a unit, stock 12' match wholesale and stock.
seed 1: enter on Apples (1/unit) coins 50->44, stock [{units 6, days_left 5}], second lot -> one batch 12, row 'stock 12'; honey batch days_left null; bread days_left 1, flowers 2.

Too few coins: honey lot with 20 coins left coins and stock unchanged, 'Not enough coins' shown and gone after next word (up). The 99-unit cap could not be reached in my runs (stock_cap 99 is in rules.json, not seen acting).
Day 1 order null; day 2 {apples,6,36} 'Order: 6 Apples for 36'; day 3 4 honey for 54; day 4 4 cheese for 66; accept -> taken true, 'Order taken: ...', second accept no change.
Run 2 on same folder: 'Slot 1: Day 1 of 7, 50 coins' and title [Day Market, New season, Continue, Records, ...].
Run with seed 9: Continue slot 1 restored seed-3 morning (wholesale, forecast, coins 50); day-2 save restored with coins 63, sign, order, stall, prices; enter on empty slot 2 stayed on slots.

Escape on morning, stall and day -> paused [Paused, Resume, Title]; clock stood at 46 while paused; Resume and Escape returned with same clock/cursor; Title -> title with slot still 50 coins after a lot bought (coins 38).
Stall opens cursor (0,0), selected apples, texts Stall, Good: Apples, Price: 4, Stock: 12, Crates: 0 of 8.
left/down at (0,0) no change; up -> y1, up stays; right x6 stops at x5; down -> (5,0).
next_good: apples,bread,cheese,fish,flowers,honey,apples; prev_good from apples -> honey; Good/Price/Stock texts follow.
put -> stall gains {x,y,good}, 'Crates: 1 of 8'; put on occupied cell no change; put with 8 crates no change; take removes; take on empty no change.
honey price_down x9 -> 1 and stops; apples price_up x9 -> 12 and stops; Price text follows.
Day-1 stall and apples price 5 carried into day 2/3; after Continue in a later run day 2 gave identical evening (needs the same stall and prices).
Enter on stall: screen day, clock 0, speed slow, texts '08:00','Speed: Slow', taken/served/walked_out/passed 0, visitors list filled.

4 day lists checked by script: ids 1..n, minutes strictly increasing in 0..479, wants distinct with counts cook 2, tourist 1, bargain 2, regular 3; same seed same list; seed 4 vs 6 gave 45 vs 66 visitors.

slow: clock +1 per 20 ticks; fast +1 per 5; rush +1 per tick; hold 57 ticks with no change on screen day; progress 36 kept across hold->rush and rush->slow (next minute after 8 slow ticks); time and Speed texts follow.
finish on day 2 -> next state evening clock 480, texts/coins/rep/stock/sales identical to the rush run.
Day 2 with slow, fast, hold, rush, slow, two pauses then finish: coins, taken, served, walked_out, passed, sales, stock, texts all equal to the all-rush run.
My own minute-by-minute model of the brief matched aisle/queue/tills/takings for all 480 minutes on 5 days (runs A, C, D, H, scan5), 0 differences; e.g. cook 7 arriving 89 at x1 at clock 90.
Same model match (front row only with empty basket, back row after a take, wants/basket checks), 0 diffs over 5 days.
Cook 7 (minute 89) holds 2 apples at 4, budget_left 32 at its arrival minute in column 0; day 2 apples at 5 and percent rule matched the model with 0 diffs.
Budget and available-units conditions in the model matched every aisle state; stock ran out with baskets never exceeding it.
passed counts and queue entry with joined = arrival+6 matched the model each minute.
Service end = start + 2 + basket entries (model with entries: 0 diffs); bargain bread 6 + flowers 7 paid 12; served, rep +1, sales entries and stock decrease matched.
Visitor 14 service ended 138 and visitor 15 leaving aisle at 138 went to the till that minute (sale 141); model with brief order matched all minutes.
No queue ever formed in any day I played (6 days, 30 seeds scanned walked_out 0), so patience, goods returned, rep -2 and walked_out +1 were never seen.
seed 3 day 1: visitor 59 (minute 474) still on aisle at 480; evening passed 45 = model at 479, not counted; screen evening at 480.
With Second till tills has two entries in the day, but no queue ever formed so two services at once / till 1 first were never seen.
Day 4 with Sign: regular 1 took honey from back cell (1,1) with empty basket at clock 2; model with sign matched (0 diffs), model without sign differs on 18 minutes.
Day 2 order 6 apples delivered: coins +36, units gone, 'Order delivered: 36'; with no apples 'Order failed' and rep 63->58; day 4 order not taken: no line, nothing changed.
Bread bought day 4 'spoiled 6' that evening; fish bought day 2 days_left 1, 'Fish: sold 0, spoiled 6' on day 3 evening; honey days_left null kept across evenings.
Heat day 4: apples days_left 4 -> 2 without Cool box, 4 -> 3 with Cool box.
Normal 7 crates 'Rent: 34', Easy 8 crates 'Rent: 31', Hard 0 crates 'Rent: 30', taken from coins.

Evening texts Evening, Day 1 of 7, Taken 125, Served 13, Walked out 0, Passed 45, per-good sold/spoiled/left matching sales and stock, Rent 34, Coins 93, Reputation 63, Tomorrow: Rain (= forecast day 2).
Upgrades texts [Upgrades, Coins: 93, Next day, Second till: 80, Cool box: 40, Sign: 30, Extra crates: 50, Awning: 35]; Next day -> morning Day 2 of 7.
Sign: coins 93->63, upgrades [sign], 'Sign: owned'; again no change; Second till with 63 -> 'Not enough coins', no change; Extra crates -> crate_limit 12, 'Crates: 5 of 12'.
Easy day with coins -1: evening 'Bankrupt', slots all null, Enter -> season_over [Bankrupt, Score: 0, Days: 1, Best: 0], record {score 0, bankrupt true}.
3-day Normal season: day 3 evening coins 25 'Season over'; Enter -> [Season over, Score: 88 (25+63), Days: 3, Best: 88]; slot emptied, title without Continue.

Records: 'Score 88, 3 days, Normal' then 'Score 0, 1 days, Easy, bankrupt'; later Hard bankrupt placed after the earlier easy tie; 6 ended seasons kept to 5; 'No records yet' on fresh; shown in later runs.

'Stamp: First coin','Stamp: Sold out' on first evening; same day replayed later on same folder showed no stamp lines; Stamps screen 'First coin: yes'... 'Rain trade: no' in a later run; stamps in stamp order.
first_coin on a paying day; full_stall on day opened with 8 crates; whole_season on the 3-day season's last evening with coins 25.
sold_out earned on day where apples/bread/flowers with crates sold to 0; honey and fish without crates on later days did not trigger it (only possible case is a good with a crate).
Day 1 and day 2 replayed after Continue (seeds 9 and 7) gave visitors, sales, coins, stock, evening texts identical to the unbroken seed-3 run.
Two copies of a kept folder, same seed 4 and script: byte-identical output; seed 6 gave another forecast, wholesale and visitor count.
escape/left/put on evening, left on title, put/finish/rush on morning, accept/finish on stall: no change seen.
data/goods.json, visitors.json, rules.json (hourly, weather, difficulty), upgrades.json, stamps.json; README 'Changing the data' says how for a good, visitor type, upgrade, stamp.
f_stall6.png: 6x2 grid, six goods in six colours (bread and cheese close), cursor outlined on (4,1), Good/Price/Crates in the text panel; crates in the right columns.

f_day2/f_day3.png: stall crates, aisle strip with visitors at x1/x3/x5 (regular large grey, cook small grey, tourist green), till block with visitor, panel with time, speed, coins, taken, served, reputation. Queue never non-empty so not seen drawn.
Frames of title, slots, settings, morning, upgrades, paused, evening, season over show their texts with '>' on the chosen row.
README has how to play (key table), where kept (--settings folder, settings.json keys), and both commands, which ran as written.

defects: Frame: the front row (y 0) is drawn at the top, farthest from the aisle strip, while the text grid in the same frame prints the back row first; the aisle is drawn next to the back row.
Bread and cheese crate colours are very close in the frames.
Quit freezes the run but the printed tick stops at the Quit tick + 1 rather than the requested tick count (as README admits).
could_not_check: d14: the 99-unit stock cap; I could not afford 17 lots of one good in any run.
d37: no queue formed in any day I ran (6 days played, 30 seeds scanned), so walk-outs never happened.
d39: no queue formed, so two tills serving at once was never seen.
